about: Which model to use for each need (a preset's 'need') and tier, in fallback order (SPEC section 6). Each row: model (an exact Higgsfield CLI id from models.json), params (generic params as the compiler names them: resolution, mode, quality, model_type...; they override the preset's size for that tier) and why. routing.py checks every row against the model's profile (durations, audio, frames, references) and puts rows that fit first. Re-check rows older than 30 days (sc.py scout check flags them).

draft_policy.why: Drafts and boards only prove the idea: no handles, the shortest allowed length that covers the shot, the smallest useful size.

upscale_policy: Upscale only when the delivery size is bigger than what the final model makes. Never upscale by default.

board.why: Vector-style marks; cheap enough to sketch with.

draft.why: Clean vector-style logos and icons with a controlled palette (--colors).
Native SVG output; fallback when Recraft misses the idea. Takes no references in SVG mode.

final.why: Same model as the approved draft keeps the look; vector output scales to any size.

icon-logo.notes: Deliver SVG (vectorise in post if the file comes back raster), then export PNG sizes from it. No upscale: vectors scale.

draft.why: Nano Banana 2: fast, cheap, good enough text to judge the layout.

final.why: Nano Banana Pro: accurate on-image text and layout.
Strong on-image text and design; transparent backgrounds.

upscale.why: Only if the delivery is bigger than 2k (print, billboards).

graphic-with-text.notes: Check every word of on-image text at final size. Thumbnails: put real text on in post when the model's text is not perfect.

board.why: Soul V2 at 1.5k: cheap faces that look real.

draft.why: Soul V2 at 1.5k: photoreal people, takes a Soul ID.

final.why: Soul Cinematic at 2k: film-grade light; add the character's Soul ID (--soul-id) for the same face in every shot.
Seedream 5 Pro at 2k: faces from reference photos, character sheets.

upscale.why: Only if the delivery is bigger than 2k.

photoreal-people.notes: Train a Soul ID (higgsfield soul-id create, 5-20 photos the user owns) for a recurring character before the drafts. Never use a real person's likeness without their consent.

board.why: Fastest, cheapest still for a composition check.

draft.why: Z Image: fastest and cheapest draft.
Nano Banana 2 at 1k when the draft needs references (the product photo).

final.why: Nano Banana Pro at 2k-4k (the preset decides): product accuracy with up to 14 references.
Seedream 5 Pro at 2k: complex scenes, edits with faces.

upscale.why: Only if the delivery is bigger than 4k (large print).

product-environment-still.notes: Product shots: pass the user's own product photo (rights owned) as a reference. Locations with no people can also try soul_location.

board.why: Image first: a cheap still proves the frame before any video credits.

draft.why: Seedance 2.0 fast at 480p, shortest length: cheap motion test in the same family as the final.
Kling 3.0 Turbo at 720p: fast, cheap simple motion.

final.why: Seedance 2.5 at 1080p: Higgsfield's default video model, 4-30 s in one take.
Seedance 2.0 when the delivery needs native 4K.

upscale.why: Only if the delivery needs more than 1080p.

video-general.notes: Approve a draft before any final. A start frame from an approved board makes the final far more predictable.

board.why: Cheap still of the key frame.

draft.why: Kling 3.0 Turbo: cheap test of the motion.

final.why: Kling 3.0 pro: strong physics, start and end frames.
Fallback for heavy motion and longer takes.

upscale.why: Only if the delivery needs more than 1080p.

video-motion-physics.notes: Sports, liquids, cloth, collisions, fast action. Kling sends sound by default: shotcraft turns it off unless the card asks for audio.

draft.why: Veo 3.1 Lite: cheap dialogue with native audio.

final.why: Veo 3.1: realistic people speaking, native sound and lip-sync.

upscale.why: Only if the delivery needs more than the model's size.

video-dialogue-audio.notes: Veo takes 4, 6 or 8 s: write lines that fit. Longer speeches are cut into several shots.

draft.why: Cinematic Studio 3.5 at low resolution: the multi-shot sequence and camera style, cheaply.

final.why: Cinematic Studio 3.5: multi-shot sequences, named camera styles, light schemes and grades.

upscale.why: Only if the delivery needs more than 1080p.

video-cinematic-multishot.notes: Always pass the duration (the model defaults to 15 s). Inline camera_style/light_scheme/color_grading cannot be mixed with style_prompt.

draft.why: Cheap motion test of an approved style frame.
Fallback draft with start and end frames for a seamless loop.

final.why: Start and end on the same frame for a loop.

mograph-loop.notes: Logos, type and UI motion are better built in your motion graphics tool (After Effects or code), outside shotcraft. Generate only textures, backgrounds and organic loops here.

board.why: Frames that need references (characters stay the same).

final.why: Boards stay cheap: 1k is enough for an animatic.

storyboard-frame.notes: Board frames are for timing and framing, not finish.

image_first.rule: A video shot starts as a cheap still (a board) when a wrong guess would waste video credits. Approve the still, then use it as the video's start frame.
applies_when: the card's tier_plan includes 'board' or the shot list flags it image-first
people or a recurring character are in frame
a product, logo or on-screen text must look exactly right
a complex camera move (orbit, crane, dolly zoom, FPV, bullet time)
the shot is long (8 s or more)
the shot needs an end frame (a match cut or a loop)
never_when: the card already has a start frame input

element_policy.about: Element sheets (characters, environments, props, style frames) are stills that take reference images. The element card's model.element wins; otherwise this default.
